units.headline: Adds 5-minute TTL for cached failed record lookups
units.summary: Adds errorCacheTTL = 5m, which sets how long GetRecord keeps returning a stored failure before it asks the server again. The comment explains it with permanently forbidden records, but the TTL covers every error.
focus: Whether 5 minutes is acceptable for transient failures, not just FORBIDDEN replies
units.reason: New tunable that decides how long lookup failures are served from cache at runtime.

units.headline: New struct holding a cached error and its expiry
units.summary: Unexported holder type pairing an error with an expiry time. It has no logic of its own; how it is used is covered in GetRecord.
units.reason: Plain unexported data type; its behavior lives in GetRecord.

units.headline: Client gains error cache map and injectable get/now funcs
units.summary: Adds an unsynchronized errors map plus get/now function fields that tests can override. The fields are unexported, so nothing on the wire changes, but the shared client now holds more mutable state.
focus: Whether the shared inventory client can be used concurrently; the maps have no lock, as before
units.reason: Struct fields added; changes the state the shared global client holds.

units.headline: NewClient initializes error cache, clock, and fetch function
units.summary: Sets up the errors map, now = time.Now, and get = fetchFromServer. Without these, GetRecord would panic on a nil map or nil func; they are set correctly.
units.reason: Plain constructor wiring of the new fields.

units.headline: GetRecord caches every failure for 5 minutes, drops retry param
units.summary: Removes the retry parameter and moves fetch and retry into c.get. Any error from the fetch is now cached per key for errorCacheTTL and returned from cache until it expires. That includes dial failures, timeouts and connection resets, not only the permanent ReplyErrors the comment talks about.
focus: Transient errors (dial failure, DeadlineExceeded) are cached the same way as FORBIDDEN
Effect together with loadMetadata now ignoring lookup errors: items are tracked without an owner

issues.title: Transient network errors cached for five minutes like permanent refusals
issues.failure_scenario: The inventory server restarts, or one request goes over the 1s requestTimeout. connect() or conn.Get fails with a dial error or i/o timeout, and that error is cached for every key looked up during the blip. For 5 minutes those keys fail without a server call. loadMetadata drops the error, so Track records those items with no owner, and the owner is never filled in later.

units.reason: Changes error and retry semantics and adds negative caching of all failures.

units.headline: Fetch reconnects once on transport errors, not on server error replies
units.summary: Moves the connect/get/retry loop out of GetRecord. It reconnects and retries once on non-reply errors and returns ReplyErrors at once without closing the connection. Before, every error, FORBIDDEN replies included, triggered a reconnect.
focus: A retry after a context deadline error fails at once because the deadline has passed; check that this is acceptable
Leaving the connection open after a ReplyError assumes the protocol stream is in sync after an ERR line
units.reason: Rewrites the retry and reconnect logic for network calls.

units.headline: Helper detects ReplyError values via errors.As
units.summary: Uses errors.As with a value-typed ReplyError, which matches how conn.Get returns it (by value). The new test covers both the plain and wrapped cases.
units.reason: Small predicate; matches the error type returned in conn.go.

units.headline: getRecord call updated to new GetRecord signature
units.summary: Drops the retry=true argument. Retrying now happens inside fetchFromServer, so the only behavior change at this call site is the one made in GetRecord.
units.reason: Call-site update for the signature change; the behavior lives in GetRecord.
